main_text.p: contentionis. Si enim effet ratio,respon-sio debuerat expectari: & sic uidere,utrū respondere deberet, an consentire ratio-nabili responsioni. Sed & hoc notādum ex eo quod dixerat, ut uideam quid loquatur in me: propheticam uisionem,& eloquium Dei, non extrinsecus ad Prophetas fieri, sed intrinsecus & interiori homini respondere. Unde & Zacharias: Et Angelus, inquit, qui loquebatur in me. Et in Psalmis: Audiam quid loquatur in me Deus. Et paulo superius: Itaque quia Propheta est, & propterea quærit, & dubitare se dicit: ut quod illi responderent, respondeatur omnibus. Hæc Hierony-mus.

head.i: Quid ergo hac oratione sibi vult Ha-bacucus Propheta?

main_text.p: Sibi, ἐν τειῷ[?] λογισμῷν[?] stanti, & summa cum admiratione intueti successus & felicitatem impiorum, & piorum ab illis op-pressorum miserias: post ἔκστασιν[?] suam, qua in disceptatione cum Deo usus erat, reue-renter petendum & exspectandum diui-num responsum, & cum nihil sit quod arguenti Deo iure obijci possit, eius iudi-cio summa cum religione standum: ac

page.notes: Running head: "VACVC" read as "VACUC"; the V is a vowel, so changed to U (HABACUC). Printed "vult" appears as "uult"; corrected to "vult" per the u/v rule. Abbreviation on "notandum" appears as "notādum"; left as printed with a macron but not certain, the mark may be a stain. Greek in the "Sibi" paragraph is partly unclear: the phrase after "ἐν" and the word after "post" are not certain and are marked [?]. The "m" at the foot is taken as the gathering signature. Possible hyphen placements (op-pressorum, reue-renter, diui-num, iudi-cio, Hierony-mus) follow the printed line breaks.
